translation: <ins>Through-wood (通木)</ins> (Instrument 6) Use fir wood three cun wide and two cun thick, its length from the waist rising past the shoulder by a little over one cun. The outside is smooth and level; on the side facing the spine, carve a concave shape, so that it fits the spine bone and the flesh of the back. Measure it in about five fen (分, read in the departing tone). The first fen: drill two holes obliquely on the left side and two holes obliquely on the right side. Passing the second fen to the third, fourth, and fifth fen, drill one hole obliquely on each of the left and right sides. Take one wide band, thread it from the upper left hole of the first fen, pass it up over the right shoulder, down the front of the chest, obliquely to the left armpit, around the back, and thread it into the second right hole of the first fen. Then use another band, thread it from the upper right hole of the first fen, pass it up over the left shoulder, down the front of the chest, obliquely to the right armpit, around the back, and thread it into the second left hole of the first fen. Both band ends are folded back and tied tightly to the wood. The third and fourth fen are also threaded with bands, passing from the soft ribs horizontally around the front of the abdomen, then back through the original holes, and tied tightly to the wood. The fifth fen is threaded with a band through its hole, wound level around the front of the abdomen, then back and tied tightly to the wood. It must not shift or move, only then is it beneficial to the affected place. Whenever this wood is used, first pad the body with cotton wadding and soft cloth, to avoid pain. Explanation of use: Whenever the back is injured by a fall or a blow, and the back bone has split open and risen high, the person will certainly be bent forward and find it hard to lie back.
